B. Is this measure already running in Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Standardised lung cancer pathway with booked slots. A lung cancer pathway on the Danish/Swedish/Norwegian model: fixed referral criteria, pre-booked CT, PET-CT, bronchoscopy and MDT slots, a named pathway owner, and published time limits for each step.
effect_summary_en: A Swedish 2023 study gives a lung cancer pathway lead time of 30–44 days, met by only 30 % of patients; it does not report how many days the pathway saved.
supported_en: Sweden's lung cancer pathway sets a lead time of 30–44 days, and 30 % of patients started treatment within it (Scientific Reports 2023).
not_supported_en: None of the pages read report how many days a lung cancer pathway saves, so the 14-day (5–23) figure is not confirmed.
summary_en: B: I found no public sign that the standardised pathway is running. The Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county pages say the lung clinic orders CT and tests case by case and that a county lung team meeting makes treatment recommendations. HUS says surgery decisions are made at Meilahti and describes ordinary referral handling, with no time limits or pre-booked slots. A: A 2023 Swedish study in Scientific Reports gives the lung cancer pathway a lead time of 30–44 days and says only 30 % of patients met it, so the 14-day saving remains an assumption.
unanswered_en: I found no Kymenhva or HUS decision, pilot or published lung cancer time limits; the HUS cancer access-times page (syovan-hoitoonpaasy) did not load.
